subject: Late-stage PoC: capacity risk window & soft-hold proposal for LynxWare
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal check — capacity for LynxWare PoC (late-stage)

Team,

Quick ask: LynxWare (LYNX-2027-1023) just entered late-stage legal review. They signalled a hard go-live target for early May if the PoC metrics look good. Sales has been pushing for a dedicated capacity plan until the first month of production.

Can infra ops confirm raw GPU headroom for the following window: May 1 — June 30? We need: 8 A100-equivalent * sustained for 12 hours/day * single-region (us-west). If we can’t guarantee capacity, we should propose a \"soft-hold\" (non-billing reservation) and communicate risk to the customer with an ETA for firm commit.

Attached I’m including the heatmap we saw in last quarter (capacity_heatmap_Q2-Q3.csv). Please call out any constraints (migrations, infra maintenance, expected client peak overlaps).

Prefer a short reply with: 1) capacity OK / partial / not available, 2) any mitigation (burst, cross-region fallback), 3) recommended customer message.

Thanks — Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachment: capacity_heatmap_Q2-Q3.csv (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal check — capacity for LynxWare PoC (late-stage)

Steph — quick summary from capacity planning after looking at the heatmap and scheduled maintenance:

- Short answer: partial availability. We can cover 6 / 8 A100-equivalent continuously for May, with 2 additional devices available via burst on preemptible/backfill nodes (up to 6 hours/day) but not for sustained 12-hour windows.
- Constraints: major scheduled kernel upgrade across clusters the week of 2027-05-09 (affects capacity by ~10% for 48 hours) and a large internal internal batch run currently slated for 2027-05-21 — that run is being re-evaluated but could knock us below the 8-device threshold for up to 6 hours.
- Mitigation: Recommend soft-hold for LynxWare for May with explicit fallback to cross-region (us-east) or scaled quantized model variant (4-bit) to reduce GPU footprint. We can also offer a limited burst SLA for first 2 weeks of production subject to a short-term prepay.

I’ll sync with Vivek on the operational playbook.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sato <emma.sato@lynxware.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@lynxware.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed soft-hold + risk window for LynxWare PoC (May 1–June 30)

Emma / Rajesh — thanks again for the productive call last week. Quick update from our end on the capacity side.

We’re proposing a short-term \"soft-hold\" for your PoC to protect availability while we finalize the contract. The soft-hold:
- Duration: May 1 — June 30 (non-billing reservation)
- Capacity: 6 guaranteed A100-equivalents sustained 12 hours/day; 2 additional devices available as burst (up to 6 hours/day) subject to cluster load
- Options if full 8 GPUs are needed for sustained windows: 1) cross-region failover (us-east) with <100ms extra RTT, 2) reduced-precision model variant (quantized) that drops GPU count by ~30% while preserving latency targets

Next steps we recommend:
1) Sign a short PO (we attached a PO template) to indicate intent — this preserves priority for capacity planning but does not start billing until production go-live.
2) Agree on an operational runbook covering maintenance windows (we’ll minimize scheduling during May if PO is accepted).

I’ve attached a short notice (lynxware_soft_hold_notice.pdf) and the PO template for procurement. Please let me know if you want us to firm up the full 8-device commitment — we can play through the pricing/discounts and a short-term prepay solution.

Regards,
Steph

Attachments: lynxware_soft_hold_notice.pdf, lynxware_po_template.pdf

From: Emma Sato <emma.sato@lynxware.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.p@lynxware.ai>
Cc: procurement@lynxware.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed soft-hold + risk window for LynxWare PoC (May 1–June 30)

Thanks Steph — the soft-hold looks sensible. A few clarifying items from procurement:

1) We understand the capacity is partial. Can you confirm whether the burst devices are preemptible and what the expected preemption frequency looks like historically?
2) If we accept the PO template and provide a signature, will Redwood guarantee that no other new customers can take those 6 guaranteed devices for the window?
3) Pricing ask: what’s the incremental cost to convert the soft-hold into a firm reserved capacity for the full 8 GPUs for May? We want to evaluate that against our internal go/no-go threshold.

We’ll review internally and aim to get the signed PO over early next week if the answers align.

— Emma
Emma Sato
Head of Platform, LynxWare

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Late-stage PoC: capacity risk window & soft-hold proposal for LynxWare

Following up on Emma's questions — answers we can share for procurement:

1) Burst devices: these are currently provided by preemptible/backfill pools. Historically, preemption that affects sustained windows in May is low (~5% chance per-day across the cluster) outside of known maintenance events. We cannot guarantee zero preemption, but for the short window we can schedule minimized risk (shift low-priority jobs) and provide a daily preemption report.

2) Guarantee on the 6 devices: if LynxWare signs the PO indicating intent to take the soft-hold, we will treat those 6 devices as reserved capacity for the window and will not reallocate them to new customer capacity requests. That reservation is operational (we’ll flag them in scheduling) but does not start billing until go-live.

3) Incremental cost to firm the full 8 GPUs: we can convert to a firm reserved capacity with a one-month minimum at an incremental price of 20% over the on-demand rate for the month of May (discounts apply for quarter commitments). If LynxWare wants a firm commitment now, we should prepare a simple SOW + invoice and propose a short prepay to lock the devices.

Recommendation: send the updated soft-hold notice (attached) and a short note to procurement answering 1–3. Marcus and I will put a checklist together for the runbook and daily preemption report.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Ops (Dedicated), Redwood Inference

Attachment: lynxware_soft_hold_notice.pdf (updated with reservation flag)
